words: يَحْذَرُ ٱلْمُنَٰفِقُونَ أَن تُنَزَّلَ عَلَيْهِمْ سُورَةٌ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An initial objection says hypocrites who did not believe the Qur'an was revealed by God could not truly fear a surah being sent down.
rows.anchor: بأن المنافقين لكفرهم في الحقيقة لم يكونوا يرون أن القرآن كلام منزل من عند الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second objection asks how a Qur'anic surah can be said to descend upon hypocrites, since they were not believers and revelation descends only upon the Prophet or believers.
rows.anchor: أنهم لما لم يكونوا مؤمنين في الواقع فكيف يصح أن يطلق أن سورة قرآنية نزلت عليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third objection says earnest inward fear cannot coexist with the claim that the hypocrites were mocking.
rows.anchor: أن حذرهم نزول السورة وهو حال داخلي جدي فيهم لا يجامع كونه استهزاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A fourth objection notes that the verse's ending seems to say God will bring out the very surah or revelation whose descent its opening says they fear.
rows.anchor: صدر الآية يذكر أنهم يحذرون أن تنزل سورة وذيلها يقول إن الله مخرج ما تحذرون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One proposed solution treats the indicative wording as an imperative, meaning let the hypocrites beware; al-Tabataba'i rejects it for lack of evidence and because the ending does not fit.
rows.anchor: إنشاء في صورة خبر أي ليحذر المنافقون أن تنزل عليهم سورة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The imperative proposal also makes the ending incoherent: telling them to beware, then saying mock and God will expose what they fear, does not mean what they ought to fear.
rows.anchor: لا معنى لقولنا ليحذر المنافقون كذا قل استهزءوا إن الله مخرج ما تحذرون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another proposal says they displayed fear mockingly rather than seriously; the author rejects it because it assumes they trusted their hidden unbelief could never be exposed.
rows.anchor: بأنهم إنما كانوا يظهرون الحذر استهزاء لا جدا وحقيقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Repeated Qur'anic disclosures of their concealed plans, together with 63:4 saying they reckon every cry is against them, undermine the claim that their fear was only mockery.
rows.anchor: وإذ كانوا شاهدوا ظهور أنبائهم ومطويات قلوبهم عيانا مرة بعد مرة

rows.speaker: جمهور المفسرين
rows.claim: Most commentators explain the fear as doubt: hypocrites who were unsure whether the prophetic call was true rationally feared a surah might expose their hearts; certainty either way would remove the fear.
rows.anchor: وهذا الجواب - وهو الذي اعتمد عليه جمهور المفسرين - وإن كان بظاهره لا يخلو عن وجه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The doubt explanation has some apparent merit, but it resolves the problem only if the verse said they feared a surah's descent; the chosen wording is not simply that construction.
rows.anchor: لو كان الواقع من التعبير في الآية نحوا من قولنا يخاف المنافقون أن تنزل عليهم سورة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Tabataba'i rejects reading the verse as an explanation for the hypocrites' earlier oath to appease believers: that detaches these verses from their independent purpose and breaks the continuous context.
rows.anchor: الآية - يحذر المنافقون الخ - ليست بيانا لسبب حلفهم المذكور سابقا بل استئناف مسوق لغرض آخر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The eleven verses form a connected unit with one purpose; earlier verses do not mention believers in a way that would license an unmarked pronoun referring back to them, which would make the discourse unclear.
rows.anchor: الآيات الإحدى عشرة. وبالجملة الآيات السابقة على هذه الآية خالية عن ذكر المؤمنين ذكرا يوجب انعطاف الذهن إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun refers to the hypocrites; describing a surah that exposes and reproaches their hypocrisy as descending upon them is acceptable even while they remain mixed among believers.
rows.anchor: والحق أن الضمير في قوله { أن تنزل عليهم } للمنافقين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an similarly speaks of revelation upon believers, People of the Book, and polytheists; such wording is no less apt for hypocrites, since scripture addresses a group's circumstances and interests.
rows.anchor: وقد أتى سبحانه بنظير هذا التعبير في أهل الكتاب حيث قال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qur'anic descent with ila or ala is common: ila highlights reaching a people, while ala evokes coming from above; either denotes the scripture addressing their affairs and benefits in this life and the next.
rows.anchor: والنزول والإنزال والتنزيل يقبل التعدي بإلى بعناية الانتهاء وبعلى بعناية الاستعلاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The argument that the command to mock proves their fear was not earnest fails: earlier revelations had already disclosed many secrets of their hearts, and the hypocrite description in 63:1 likewise bears on the point.
rows.anchor: أن قوله تعالى { قل استهزءوا } دليل أنهم كانوا يستهزءون بالحذر ولم يكن من جد الحذر في شيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Earlier revelations in al-Baqara, al-Nisa', and other surahs exposed the hypocrites' concealed thoughts, supporting the view that their fear was genuine rather than sarcastic.
rows.anchor: الآيات الكثيرة النازلة في سورة البقرة والنساء وغيرها - وكل ذلك قبل هذه الآيات نزولا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The following words are God's direct address to the hypocrites, shifting from the Prophet's address to them; the shift conveys intense anger and personally threatens unavoidable punishment.
rows.anchor: فيكون التفاتا من خطاب النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم إلى خطابهم والنكتة فيه إظهار كمال الغضب

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some commentators treat 9:67 as a fresh description of hypocrites' shared traits and fate, followed by a matching description of believers; 9:68's pairing of hypocrites and disbelievers supports their reading.
rows.anchor: ذكروا أنه استئناف يتعرض لحال عامة المنافقين بذكر أوصافهم العامة الجامعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author instead reads 9:67 as explaining why God may punish one group after saying he may pardon another: all hypocrites share corrupt traits, deeds, and ultimate recompense, so this is not punishment of neighbors for one another's acts.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أن الآية في مقام التعليل لقوله في الآية السابقة { إن نعف عن طائفة منكم نعذب طائفة }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase expresses a common inner constitution that unifies the hypocrites despite their plurality and makes them share qualities, actions, and the recompense promised by God.
rows.anchor: المنافقين جميعا بعضهم من بعض لاشتراكهم في خبائث الصفات والأعمال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mentioning hypocrite women although none were previously mentioned emphasizes the unity of their disposition with the men and signals women's active place in the corrupt hypocritical society.
rows.anchor: ولعله ذكر المنافقات مع المنافقين مع عدم سبق لذكرهن للدلالة على كمال الاتحاد والاتفاق بينهم

words: يَأْمُرُونَ بِٱلْمُنكَرِ وَيَنْهَوْنَ عَنِ ٱلْمَعْرُوفِ وَيَقْبِضُونَ أَيْدِيَهُمْ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hypocrites promote wrong, obstruct right, and hold back spending in God's path; these habits express their turning away from remembering God and their departure from servitude.
rows.anchor: فهم { يأمرون بالمنكر وينهون عن المعروف } ويمسكون عن الإنفاق في سبيل الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Forgetting God means turning away from his remembrance; God's forgetting them means withholding the reward he gives servants mindful of their Lord.
rows.anchor: نسوا الله تعالى بالإعراض عن ذكره لأنهم فاسقون خارجون عن زي العبودية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God joins disbelievers to hypocrites because they are alike, promising them abiding Hell as sufficient punishment, God's curse, and lasting torment.
rows.anchor: وعطف عليهم الكفار لأنهم جميعا سواء - نار جهنم خالدين فيها هي حسبهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Enjoining right, forbidding wrong, and spending in God's path all count as remembrance of God.
rows.anchor: ويتفرع على ذلك أن الأمر بالمعروف والنهي عن المنكر والإنفاق في سبيل الله من الذكر

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Raghib defines khalaq as the virtue a person acquires through their character; other commentators take it to mean a share without qualification.
rows.anchor: قال الراغب الخلاق ما اكتسبه الإنسان من الفضيلة بخلقه

rows.speaker: غيره
rows.claim: Other lexicographers explain khalaq as an unrestricted share or allotment.
rows.anchor: وفسره غيره بمطلق النصيب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The comparison continues the direct address to hypocrites begun at 9:66 and illustrates that they and earlier disbelievers share a nature of turning from God and pursuing worldly enjoyment.
rows.anchor: والآية من تتمة مخاطبة المنافقين التي في قوله { لا تعتذروا قد كفرتم بعد إيمانكم } الآية في سياق واحد متصل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Earlier communities enjoyed their worldly allotments and plunged into God's signs; like them, the hypocrites will have their deeds annulled in both worlds and suffer loss.
rows.anchor: الإقبال على الاستمتاع بما أوتوا من أعراض الدنيا من أموال وأولاد والخوض في آيات الله

words: كَانُوا۟ أَشَدَّ مِنكُمْ قُوَّةً وَأَكْثَرَ أَمْوَٰلًا وَأَوْلَٰدًا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The predecessors' greater strength and wealth did not protect them from God or prevent loss; the present hypocrites, weaker and poorer, have even less reason to expect escape.
rows.anchor: أنهم لم يعجزوا الله بذلك، ولم يدفع ذلك عنهم غائلة الحبط والخسران

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Noah's people drowned; Ad, the people of Hud, were destroyed by a violent wind; Thamud, the people of Salih, were punished by an earthquake; Nimrod's people lost their blessing; Lot's overturned towns were destroyed.
rows.anchor: فذاك قوم نوح عمهم الله سبحانه بالغرق، وعاد وهم قوم هود أهلكهم بريح صرصر عاتية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-mu'tafikat are Lot's towns turned upside down; the word derives from the earth overturning.
rows.anchor: والمؤتفكات وهي القرى المنقلبات على وجهها - من ائتفكت الأرض إذا انقلبت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase summarizes their histories: messengers brought clear signs, they denied them, and destruction followed; God did not wrong them, since they themselves chose worldly indulgence, disputing signs, and rejecting messengers.
rows.anchor: فكذبوها فانتهى أمرهم إلى الهلاك، ولم يكن من شأن السنة الإلهية أن يظلمهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Believers, despite differences of number and gender, form one unified community; therefore they mutually assume responsibility for and manage one another's affairs.
rows.anchor: ليدل بذلك على أنهم مع كثرتهم وتفرقهم من حيث العدد ومن الذكورة والأنوثة ذوو كينونة واحدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because this mutual guardianship extends throughout the community, believers enjoin right and forbid wrong among one another as well.
rows.anchor: فلولاية بعض المجتمع على بعض ولاية سارية في جميع الابعاض دخل في تصديقهم الأمر بالمعروف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prayer and zakat are the two firm pillars of the law: prayer links God and creation through worship, while zakat links people through social dealings.
rows.anchor: فالصلاة ركن العبادات التي هي الرابطة بين الله وبين خلقه، والزكاة في المعاملات التي هي رابطة بين الناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Obedience to God gathers all divine legal rulings; obedience to the Messenger gathers his authoritative rulings for governing and reforming the community, including campaigns, judgments, and legal penalties.
rows.anchor: فجمع في إطاعة الله جميع الأحكام الشرعية الإلهية وجمع في إطاعة رسوله جميع الأحكام الولائية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In another respect, obeying God's revealed laws is included in obeying the Messenger, who proclaims truth and calls people to the fundamentals and branches of religion.
rows.anchor: على أن إطاعة شرائع الله النازلة من السماء من جهة أخرى منطوية في إطاعة الرسول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The promise reports God's decree that his mercy encompasses people described by these qualities and mirrors the hypocrites' being forgotten by God.
rows.anchor: وكأن في هذه الجملة محاذاة لما سرد في المنافقين من قوله تعالى { نسوا الله فنسيهم }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's might cannot obstruct his mercy, and his wisdom entails no defect, weakness, or arbitrary judgment; these attributes explain the promised mercy.
rows.anchor: فلا مانع من رحمته لعزته، ولا اختلال أو وهنا وجزافا في حكمته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Adn means staying and settling; gardens of Eden are gardens of residence, stability, and lasting permanence.
rows.anchor: العدن مصدر بمعنى الإقامة والاستقرار يقال عدن بالمكان أي أقام فيه واستقر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's approval is greater than all the gardens and dwellings; the indefinite form may suggest an approval beyond human measure, or that even a little of it exceeds every other reward.
rows.anchor: وقد نكر { رضوان } إيماء إلى أنه لا يقدر بقدر ولا يحيط به وهم بشر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The point is not merely that every blessing flows from God's approval; true servitude is love of God rather than pursuit of paradise or fear of hell, and the lover most desires the beloved's approval.
rows.anchor: بل لأن حقيقة العبودية التي يندب إليها كتاب الله هي عبوديته تعالى حبا له لا طمعا في جنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The concluding wording restricts great success to this divine approval: without some reality of God's approval, the pleasures of paradise would be punishment rather than blessing.
rows.anchor: أي أن هذا الرضوان هو حقيقة كل فوز عظيم حتى الفوز العظيم بالجنة الخالدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reports create a further difficulty because they depict verses as fragmented, each revealed for a separate occasion and purpose, whereas the passage has one continuous context and aim.
rows.anchor: ظهورها في تقطع الآيات وتشتت بعضها وانفصاله عن بعض بنزول كل لسبب آخر

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbi reports that on the return from Tabuk three men mocked God, the Messenger, and the Qur'an, while Yazid ibn Wadi'a stayed apart; 9:66 then descended, making him the single person called a ta'ifa.
rows.anchor: عن الكلبي أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم لما أقبل من غزوة تبوك وبين يديه ثلاثة رهط استهزءوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This story underlies some commentators' claim that ta'ifa can mean one person as well as a group; the author says the verse uses it as a metonymy, not as a label for that individual.
rows.anchor: وهذا هو منشأ قول بعضهم إن الطائفة تطلق على الواحد كما تطلق على الكثير

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that hypocrites travelling to Tabuk mocked the coming fight, Makshi ibn Humayr wished for a hundred lashes to avoid revelation, and the Prophet sent Ammar to confront them; after excuses, 9:66 was revealed, and God pardoned Makshi, who later died at Yamama unknown.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال نزلت هذه الآية في رهط من المنافقين من بني عمرو بن عوف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although Makshi's story appears in several reports, even if authentic it does not establish that these verses were revealed about it; the gap between the story and the verses' content is too wide to let such anecdotes dictate interpretation.
rows.anchor: على تقدير صحتها لا تستلزم نزول الآيات فيها على ما بينها وبين مضامين الآيات من البون البعيد

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas compares the community to the Israelites, saying they will follow their predecessors so closely that they would enter a lizard's burrow if one of them did.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال ما أشبه الليلة بالبارحة { كالذين من قبلكم كانوا أشد منكم قوة }

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet predicts that Muslims will follow earlier peoples span by span—even into a lizard's hole—and, when asked if he means Persians, Romans, or the People of the Book, replies that they are the people in question.
rows.anchor: عن أبي هريرة عن أبي سعيد الخدري عن النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم قال لتأخذن كما أخذت الأمم

rows.speaker: حذيفة
rows.claim: Hudhayfa says the hypocrites living then were worse than those in the Prophet's time: the earlier ones hid their hypocrisy, while these make it public.
rows.anchor: عن حذيفة قال المنافقون الذين فيكم اليوم شر من المنافقين الذين كانوا على عهد رسول الله

rows.speaker: الرضا عليه السلام
rows.claim: Al-Rida says God neither forgets nor slips; forgetting by God means recompensing those who forgot him by making them forget themselves or leaving them as they neglected preparation for meeting him, as 19:64, 39:19, and 45:34 explain.
rows.anchor: قال سألت الرضا عليه السلام عن قول الله عز وجل { نسوا الله فنسيهم } فقال إن الله تبارك وتعالى لا ينسى

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر عليه السلام
rows.claim: Abu Ja'far explains that they forgot God by abandoning obedience, and God forgot them by abandoning them.
rows.anchor: عن جابر عن أبي جعفر عليه السلام { نسوا الله } قال تركوا طاعة الله { فنسيهم } قال فتركهم

rows.speaker: علي عليه السلام
rows.claim: Ali says they forgot God in worldly life by not obeying or believing in him and his Messenger; God forgets them in the afterlife by granting no share in his reward, leaving them deprived of good.
rows.anchor: عن أبي معمر السعداني قال قال علي عليه السلام في قوله { نسوا الله فنسيهم } فإنما يعني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author notes that al-Saduq also transmits Ali's explanation in Ma'ani through Abu Ma'mar.
rows.anchor: أقول ورواه الصدوق في المعاني بإسناده عن أبي معمر عنه عليه السلام

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
rows.claim: Abu Abd Allah identifies the overturned towns as Lot's people, whose land was flipped so its upper part became lower.
rows.anchor: عن أبي بصير عن أبي عبد الله عليه السلام - في حديث - قلت { والمؤتفكات أتتهم رسلهم بالبينات } قال

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
rows.claim: Abu Abd Allah permits Safwan to transport a Muslim woman he knows when she has no mahram, saying a believer is a mahram for a believing woman, and recites this verse.
rows.anchor: عن صفوان بن مهران قال قلت لأبي عبد الله عليه السلام تأتيني المرأة المسلمة قد عرفتني بعملي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author notes that al-Ayyashi also transmits the Safwan al-Jammal report from Abu Abd Allah.
rows.anchor: أقول ورواه العياشي في تفسيره عن صفوان الجمال عنه عليه السلام

rows.speaker: علي بن الحسين عليهما السلام
rows.claim: Ali ibn al-Husayn describes the believer's ease and abundance in paradise: attendants serve them, fruit hangs nearby, springs and rivers flow, furnishings are laid out, and whatever they desire arrives before they ask.
rows.anchor: عن ثوير عن علي بن الحسين عليهما السلام قال إذا صار أهل الجنة في الجنة ودخل ولي الله إلى جناته

rows.speaker: علي بن الحسين عليهما السلام
rows.claim: In the continuation of Ali ibn al-Husayn's report, God asks the people of paradise whether they want anything better; he says his approval and love surpass their pleasures, and the Imam recites 9:72.
rows.anchor: فيعود عليهم القول فيقولون ربنا نعم فأتنا بخير مما نحن فيه

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet reports that after the people enter paradise, God asks if they wish for more; they say everything has been granted, and God says his approval means he will never be displeased with them.
rows.anchor: عن جابر قال قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إذا دخل أهل الجنة الجنة قال الله هل تشتهون شيئا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author says this meaning appears in many reports transmitted by both Sunni and Shi'i channels.
rows.anchor: أقول وهذا المعنى وارد في روايات كثيرة من طرق الفريقين

rows.speaker: أبو الدرداء
rows.claim: Abu al-Darda reports from the Prophet that Eden is God's unseen abode, entered only by prophets, the truthful, and martyrs, and blessed is whoever enters it.
rows.anchor: عن أبي الدرداء عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم عدن دار الله التي لم ترها عين ولم تخطر على قلب بشر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: That report's restricted list does not conflict with the verse's generality, since 57:19 indicates that God will join the broader body of believers to the truthful and martyrs.
rows.anchor: ولا ينافي خصوص سكنة الجنة في الرواية عمومهم في الآية لدلالة قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر عليه السلام
rows.claim: Abu Ja'far explains the command to strive against disbelievers and hypocrites as enforcing religious obligations.
rows.anchor: عن أبي بصير عن أبي جعفر عليه السلام قال جاهد الكفار والمنافقين بإلزام الفرائض

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Mas'ud reports that after this verse was revealed, the Prophet ordered striving by hand, then heart, then tongue, and finally meeting the target with a stern face if unable to do more.
rows.anchor: عن ابن مسعود قال لما نزلت { يا أيها النبي جاهد الكفار والمنافقين } أمر رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author finds the report's ordering confused because striving by heart comes after the other means, with intervening material separating it.
rows.anchor: وفي الرواية تشويش من حيث ترتب أجزائها فالجهاد بالقلب بعد الجميع

words: فَلَمَّآ ءَاتَىٰهُم مِّن فَضْلِهِۦ بَخِلُوا۟ بِهِۦ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One group of poor hypocrites promised to give charity and be righteous if enriched, then became miserly and turned away when God gave them wealth; other hypocrites criticized both affluent and poor believers who donated, and God judged them all hypocrites and beyond forgiveness.
rows.anchor: بيان تذكر الآيات طائفة أخرى من المنافقين تخلفوا عن حكم الصدقات فامتنعوا عن إيتاء الزكاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ita' means giving; the phrase giving from God's bounty often means granting wealth here, as shown by the promise to give charity and the next verse's mention of miserliness.
rows.anchor: الإيتاء الإعطاء، وقد كثر إطلاق الإيتاء من الفضل على إعطاء المال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The context presents a real event, and the reports say these verses were revealed about Tha'laba; the author defers the story to the following report discussion and says the verses' meaning is clear.
rows.anchor: والروايات تدل على أن الآيات نزلت في ثعلبة في قصة سيأتي نقلها في البحث الروائي التالي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Aqaba means to cause or leave something in succession; al-Majma' treats it as synonymous with bequeathing or handing down, and it can also mean requiting.
rows.anchor: الإعقاب الإيراث قال في المجمع وأعقبه وأورثه وأداه نظائر وقد يكون أعقبه بمعنى جازاه

words: فَأَعْقَبَهُم نِفَاقًا فِي قُلُوبِهِمْ إِلَىٰ يَوْمِ يَلْقَوْنَهُ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun in 'so it caused them' may refer to miserliness itself or to their deed, including miserliness; on that reading, the day they meet is figuratively the day they meet its recompense.
rows.anchor: والضمير في قوله { فأعقبهم } راجع إلى البخل أو إلى فعلهم الذي منه البخل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively the pronoun refers to God and the day of meeting him is the Resurrection or death; death is more fitting, since one naturally says their hypocrisy lasts until they die rather than until resurrection, and 29:5 uses meeting God for death.
rows.anchor: وهذا الثاني هو الظاهر على الثاني لأن الأنسب عند الذهن أن يقال فهم على نفاقهم إلى أن يموتوا

words: بِمَآ أَخْلَفُوا۟ ٱللَّهَ مَا وَعَدُوهُ وَبِمَا كَانُوا۟ يَكْذِبُونَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Both occurrences of bi are causal: the miserliness produced hypocrisy because it involved breaking their promise to God and persisting in lies, which made inner and outer selves diverge.
rows.anchor: الباء في الموضعين منه للسببية أي إن هذا البخل أورثهم نفاقا بما كان فيه من الخلف في الوعد

words: بِمَآ أَخْلَفُوا۟ ٱللَّهَ مَا وَعَدُوهُ وَبِمَا كَانُوا۟ يَكْذِبُونَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse indicates that breaking promises and habitual lying are causes and signs of hypocrisy.
rows.anchor: وفي الآية دلالة أولا على أن خلف الوعد وكذب الحديث من أسباب النفاق وأماراته
